title: Wintergrasp
body: Wintergrasp is a frozen valley in west-central Northrend, ringed by the Borean Tundra, Sholazar Basin, Icecrown and the Dragonblight. Titan fortifications dot the land and elemental riches abound, and both make it a prize: elementals of air, earth, water, fire and shadow roam it, and even living plants. At its northern end stands Wintergrasp Fortress, which guards the way into the Vault of Archavon, and the Valiance Expedition of the Alliance and the Horde's Warsong champions fight over it again and again, in what the call to arms names the Battle for Lake Wintergrasp. No victory here is more than temporary. Between battles one side garrisons the keep while the other gathers at a camp on the valley's edge, and when war returns, goblin and gnomish engineers turn out catapults, demolishers and siege engines at workshops across the field. The Wintergrasp River cuts the valley in two, with three towers beyond it to the south, and even in the lulls soldiers of both sides scour the land for embers, bone, herbs and armor, and kill each other for them.

title: Wintergrasp Fortress
body: Wintergrasp Fortress stands at the northern end of the valley, the prize every battle is fought for. Two rings of walls guard it, broken by a great gate and anchored by four towers at its corners. Within lie two goblin workshops that can never be taken from the defenders, the officers and quartermasters of whichever side holds the place, and portals to distant battlefields. Behind the keep's innermost door lies the chamber where, in battle, an attacking army must claim the titan relic to win the fortress. Here too opens the way into the Vault of Archavon, which only the side holding the fortress may enter.

title: The Wintergrasp River
body: The Wintergrasp River runs east to west across the middle of the valley and splits the field in two: the fortress and the nearer workshops on its northern side, the southern towers and the two farthest workshops beyond it. Three crossings span it, the Western, Central and Eastern Bridges, linking the two halves of the battlefield. Between battles the banks are quiet but not safe: glacial spirits drift along the water, and saronite crops out among the stones.

title: The Southern Towers
body: South of the Wintergrasp River stand three fortified towers: Shadowsight Tower in the west, Winter's Edge Tower in the south and Flamewatch Tower in the east. In every battle they stand with the army besieging the fortress, and they are built so stoutly that only siege engines can bring one down. Between battles they stand silent over the southern field, and whispering winds drift past their walls.

parts.body: The towers are more than strongpoints. The officers of the fortress say they draw power away from it, and when one is brought down that power can be turned back into the titan relic to strengthen the fortress's own soldiers. So the defenders do not simply wait behind their walls: they cross the river and topple a tower where the attackers least expect it.

title: The Siege Workshops
body: Six goblin workshops build the siege engines of Wintergrasp. Two stand inside the fortress walls and never change hands. The other four lie out on the field: the Broken Temple in the west and the Sunken Ring in the east, nearer the fortress, and Westspark and Eastspark in the far south beyond the river. Each flies a banner that can be torn down and raised for the other side, and keeps a graveyard with a spirit guide, taunka for the Horde, dwarven for the Alliance. Goblin mechanics build for the Horde and gnomish engineers for the Alliance, turning out catapults, demolishers and siege engines for soldiers of rank enough to authorize one, while the parts last.

title: The Cauldron of Flames
body: In the southeast of Wintergrasp lies the Cauldron of Flames, a burning hollow where raging flames and drifting cinder clouds roam among the rocks. It yields eternal embers, which the siegesmiths of both sides mix with coal to fuel their demolishers and siege engines. Between battles soldiers of the Alliance and the Horde come here to gather them, and as often as not they take the embers from each other's bodies. The Horde's Siegesmith Stronghoof tells his soldiers that if the enemy has already gone, they must fight the fire elementals until they find some.

title: Glacial Falls
body: Glacial Falls spills down the eastern side of Wintergrasp, cold water and ice where glacial spirits drift. The Alliance's enchantress, Sorceress Kaylana, says her research shows that the armor of soldiers lately slain here comes away steeped in energy, and the Horde's Hoodoo Master Fu'jin claims the falls can draw out a strong warrior's soul, which he means to bind into his wards and jinxes. So both sides send soldiers to kill each other at the falls, and when no enemy can be found, they strip the armor of adventurers the elementals have killed.

title: The Forest of Shadows
body: On the western edge of Wintergrasp lies the Forest of Shadows, a dark wood littered with old dragon bones and haunted by wandering shadows. Some say the spirits impale their living victims on the bones as they die. The bones are useful all the same: with dragonbone grown hard to come by in the Dragonblight, the bowyers of both sides need splinters from this forest for their arrowheads, and their soldiers come hunting for them, and for each other. Bowyer Randolph of the Alliance has heard it is haunted, and admits he never goes there himself.

title: The Steppe of Life
body: In the southwest of Wintergrasp, the Steppe of Life is a stretch of ground where things still grow despite the cold, guarded by living lashers that whip at anyone who comes too close. Both sides' healers depend on it. The Horde's Primalist Mulfort makes salve for the wounded from the roses that grow here, and the Alliance's Anchorite Tessa grinds its herbs into a medicine against the cold. Mulfort complains that the Alliance strips the roses too fast, Tessa that the Horde has been gathering the herbs, so soldiers come to gather and stay to kill one another, and Tessa still warns of the lashers that gave a Private Doane a fine whipping.

title: Commander Zanneth
body: Commander Zanneth leads the Alliance's fighters in Wintergrasp. He greets each newcomer as one come to serve the sons of Azeroth in battle, and whether he stands in the fortress or at the camp from which the Alliance marches on it, his orders never change: go out, defeat ten of the Horde's finest, and come back. Not all his officers think that enough. Tactical Officer Ahbramis grumbles that the commander might be content with a pile of Horde corpses at his feet, while what matters to the Valiance Expedition is who holds Wintergrasp.

title: Commander Dardosh
body: Commander Dardosh leads the Horde's fighters in Wintergrasp, and he greets each newcomer with a war cry and a question: have they come to serve the Horde in battle? Whether he stands in the fortress or at the camp from which the Horde marches on it, he carries Warlord Garrosh's orders, and Garrosh asks only one thing: that every foe be slain. Every recruit is sent out to bring down ten of the Alliance's strongest. Tactical Officer Kilrath, at his side, takes a longer view: Dardosh may be content with slain foes, but what matters to Kilrath is holding the fortress itself.

title: The Battle for Wintergrasp
body: At set times the war for Wintergrasp breaks out anew. The defenders muster inside the fortress, while the attackers gather at their camp and march on it. The workshops pour out siege engines, and each side's officers give their soldiers the task their role demands. The attackers must crew and guard their machines while they smash wall after wall; the Alliance trusts in what Senior Demolitionist Legoso calls the power of gnomish technology, and the Horde's Lieutenant Murp wishes he could leave camp to smash walls himself. The defenders must wreck those machines before they break through. The attackers' goal lies deep in the keep, where they must claim the titan relic before time runs out; if they fail, the fortress stays in the defenders' hands.

parts.body: A victory in Wintergrasp has been won, and it will not be the last battle. Whoever holds the fortress must hold it again when the war returns, and whoever lost it will come back for it. The Alliance's officers count even a passing victory crucial to their whole strategy against the Horde, and the Horde's officers honor those who fought for it as having done a truly great thing.

title: The Elementals of Wintergrasp
body: Wintergrasp swarms with elementals. Chilled earth elementals lumber across the open valley, and glacial spirits haunt the river, the falls and the Chilled Quagmire. Whispering winds drift through the south, raging flames and cinder clouds burn in the Cauldron of Flames, wandering shadows stalk the Forest of Shadows, and living lashers guard the Steppe of Life. They answer to neither the Alliance nor the Horde and turn on whoever strays near them, so anyone who crosses the valley between battles must reckon with them as well as with the enemy.

The revenants and Mature Lashers (phase 256) are left out and are not triggers. ACCEPT of the weeklies not used.

parts.body: The elementals are part of why the valley is worth fighting for, since it is rich in elemental materials. Between battles both armies send soldiers out to gather: embers from the fire, armor from the falls, bone from the shadowed forest and herbs from the lashers' steppe. The quartermasters would rather their soldiers took these things from enemy bodies, but when no enemy is about, the elementals and their victims will serve.
sources: quests 13153, 13198, 13192, 13202 (armor of adventurers slain by the elementals), 13191, 13200 (fight the fire elementals for embers), 13193, 13199 (bones from the spirits), 13195, 13194, 13201 (a lasher might have one); every gathering quest asks first for the enemy's bodies
